questions.question: What is meant by the term "climate" when discussing a specific location?
options: The daily changes in wind speed and cloud cover
The average weather conditions over a long period of time
The atmospheric pressure recorded at any single moment
The immediate temperature and precipitation on a given day

questions.question: Based on scientific data, what trend is predicted for extreme weather events as the global temperature continues to rise?
options: They will become less frequent but much longer in duration
They will happen with an increased frequency
They will cease to occur entirely in equatorial regions
They will maintain a perfectly stable, predictable cycle

questions.question: Which of the following stages in the life cycle of food contributes to its total carbon footprint?
options: Only the cooking process in domestic kitchens
Land-use change, farming, processing, transport, retail, and packaging
Only the final decomposition of leftovers in domestic compost bins
None, as carbon footprint is only associated with heavy industrial manufacturing

questions.question: When comparing food types, what is generally true about the carbon footprints of meat products and plant-based products?
options: They are exactly identical because all organic matter contains carbon
Meat products and plant-based products have different carbon footprints
Plant-based products always have a higher footprint because plants respire carbon dioxide
Soil quality is the only factor, making the food type itself irrelevant

questions.question: How can changing our dietary choices and reducing food waste help us eat more sustainably?
options: By increasing the total amount of plastic packaging required
By lowering greenhouse gas emissions associated with food production
By forcing farmers to use more synthetic fertilisers to meet demand
By ensuring that food transport distances are maximised

questions.question: What do temperature data from the last century or so show about the Earth's average surface temperature?
options: A steady and predictable decrease in temperatures worldwide
An unusual, rapid increase in the average surface temperature
Absolutely no change from the temperatures of previous millennia
Fluctuations that only occur in the southern hemisphere

questions.question: What relationship has been observed between historical temperature data and data on greenhouse gas emissions?
options: There is a correlation showing that as greenhouse gas emissions increase, temperatures also increase
There is a negative correlation, meaning higher emissions lead to colder surface temperatures
There is no observable relationship or correlation between the two sets of data
The data show that temperature rises happen centuries before emissions begin to change

questions.question: How do thermal insulators help make a building more energy-efficient?
options: They generate extra heat energy through chemical reactions in the walls
They reduce the energy needed to heat the building by slowing down heat loss
They convert solar radiation directly into electrical energy
They increase the rate at which warm air is ventilated out of the rooms

questions.question: How do thermostats contribute to reducing energy use in a home?
options: They automatically turn off all electrical appliances when not in use
They control temperature automatically in different rooms to help reduce unnecessary heating
They physically block draughts from entering through windows and doors
They convert cold air into warm air without using any energy

questions.question: Why do renewable energy resources not run out?
options: Because they are replenished faster than they are used up
Because they are stored in infinite quantities deep inside the Earth's core
Because humans have banned the consumption of these resources
Because they only exist in countries near the equator where the sun is strongest

questions.question: Under what condition is a resource like wood considered renewable?
options: It is always renewable under any circumstances because trees grow naturally
Only if it is used sustainably, ensuring new trees are grown to replace those cut down
Only if it is chemically treated to prevent decomposition
It is never renewable because once a tree is cut down, that wood cannot be reused

questions.question: Why is it impossible to have a sustainable transport system that relies on petrol or diesel fuel?
options: Because petrol and diesel engines are too quiet to be safe for pedestrians
Because petrol and diesel are fossil fuels that release greenhouse gases and cannot be replenished
Because petrol and diesel vehicles cannot travel long distances
Because these fuels are too expensive for local councils to purchase

questions.question: What is the main benefit of the natural greenhouse effect for life on Earth?
options: It blocks all solar radiation from reaching the surface of the planet
It maintains an optimal temperature range for life to survive and thrive
It prevents the formation of storms and other extreme weather events
It keeps the atmosphere completely free of carbon dioxide and water vapour

questions.question: Why do waste management sites, such as landfills and incinerators, contribute to climate change?
options: They release large amounts of oxygen which cools the atmosphere too quickly
They are sources of greenhouse gases
They absorb solar radiation and trap it permanently in the soil
They prevent the natural cycle of rain from occurring in local areas

questions.question: What is the primary long-term goal of using resources sustainably?
options: To ensure that resources are available for future generations
To use up all available resources as quickly as possible to boost the economy
To replace all natural resources with synthetic, man-made materials
To prevent any future scientific development or industrial progress
